examples.en: I learned Darwin's theory of evolution at school.
I'm reading a book about the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 진화론은 생물이 환경에 맞게 변해 왔다고 설명해요.
examples.en: The theory of evolution explains that living things have changed to fit their environment.
There was a long debate over the theory of evolution.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에서는 진화론을 쉽게 소개해 줘요.
examples.en: This museum introduces the theory of evolution in an easy way.

examples.ko: 진화론이 나오기 전에는 사람들이 다르게 생각했어요.
examples.en: Before the theory of evolution appeared, people thought differently.

explain: '진화'는 실제로 일어나는 변화를 말하고, '진화론'은 그 변화를 다룬 이론을 말해요. 그래서 '진화가 일어나다'처럼 쓰지만, 이론은 '진화론이 나오다', '진화론을 배우다'처럼 써요. 보통 '창조론'과 짝으로 나오고, '다윈의 진화론'처럼 사람 이름과 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: We learned about the theory of evolution in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업에서 이론을 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying the theory in class.
phrases.en_equiv: to learn the theory of evolution

phrases.en: Darwin put forward the theory of evolution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이론을 내세우는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person advancing the theory.
phrases.en_equiv: to advocate the theory of evolution

phrases.en: We debated the theory of evolution and creationism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝이 되는 말과 함께 두 생각을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired to compare the two views.

explain_en: '진화' is the change that actually happens, while '진화론' is the theory about that change. So you say '진화가 일어나다' for the change itself, but '진화론이 나오다' or '진화론을 배우다' for the theory. It often appears paired with '창조론' (creationism), and commonly with a person's name, as in '다윈의 진화론'.

en: to be started; to be commenced

examples.en: The new construction gets under way next week.
A week has passed since the investigation began.
Once the project starts, the team will get busy.
The recovery work began right away yesterday.
When the investigation began, people took notice.
There is only a plan; work hasn't begun yet.

explain: 착수되다는 공사, 조사, 수사, 연구처럼 큰일이 실제로 시작될 때 써요. '시작되다'보다 격식이 있고 공식적인 일에 어울려요. 파티나 수업이 시작될 때는 '시작되다'를 써요. 시작하는 쪽은 '착수하다'예요.

phrases.en: The new construction starts next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '착수되다'보다 덜 격식적이고 어떤 일에든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than 착수되다 and usable for any kind of event.

phrases.en: An investigation into the cause of the accident was launched right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사, 수사, 공사처럼 공식적인 일과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing with official matters like investigations and construction.

phrases.example: 공사가 착수되기 전에 주민들에게 알려야 해요.
phrases.en: We have to notify residents before the construction begins.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 전에'와 연결해서 일이 시작되기 앞선 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connected with -기 전에 to talk about the time before the work begins.

explain_en: 착수되다 is used when a sizable job such as construction, an investigation or research actually begins. It is more formal than 시작되다 and suits official matters. For a party or a class starting, use 시작되다. The active form is 착수하다.

en: to be interpreted; to be comprehended; to be explained

examples.en: This sentence can be interpreted in two ways.
His words were interpreted as a refusal.
I wonder how dreams are interpreted.
The results may be interpreted differently.
It's an expression that doesn't read naturally when translated.
I corrected the content that had been misinterpreted.

explain: 말이나 글이 어떤 뜻으로 이해될 때 써요. '~로 해석되다'가 기본 틀이고, 같은 말을 사람마다 다르게 받아들일 때 자주 나와요. 다른 언어로 옮기는 것은 '번역되다'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: This poem is interpreted differently by each person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들이는 방식이 사람마다 다를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when people understand something in different ways.

phrases.example: 그 말은 긍정적으로 해석될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: That remark can be interpreted positively.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~로 해석되다' 틀에 '긍정적으로'를 넣은 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ~로 해석되다 pattern with 긍정적으로 filled in.

phrases.en: This sentence is not easy to interpret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻을 이해하기 어려울 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when the meaning is hard to understand.

explain_en: Use it when words or writing get understood in a certain way. The basic frame is ~로 해석되다, and it often appears when people read the same thing differently. Moving it into another language is 번역되다, which is a separate word.

en: to be released (film); to be unsealed

examples.en: That movie will be released next week.

examples.ko: 개봉된 지 일주일 만에 백만 명이 봤어요.
examples.en: A million people saw it within a week of its release.

examples.ko: 포장이 이미 개봉되어 있어서 환불이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The package has already been opened, so a refund is not possible.

examples.ko: 새 영화가 개봉되는 날 친구와 극장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I will go to the theater with a friend on the day the new film opens.
I watched the trailer before the film was released.
I rewatched a movie that was released last year.

explain: 영화가 처음 극장에서 상영될 때 주로 '개봉되다'를 써요. 이미 한 번 나온 영화를 다시 올리면 '재개봉'이라고 해요. 포장을 연다는 뜻은 쇼핑에서 '개봉 상품', '미개봉'으로 자주 써요. 상자나 편지를 여는 일은 '열다', '뜯다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 다음 달에 개봉될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: That movie is scheduled to be released next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 극장에서 곧 나올 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a film that will soon come out in theaters.

phrases.en: Unopened items can be refunded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장을 열지 않은 상품을 말하는 쇼핑 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shopping word for goods whose package has not been opened.

phrases.en: The theater released a new movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개봉되다'의 능동형이에요. 상자를 연다는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form of 개봉되다, and it can also mean opening a package.

explain_en: Mostly used when a film first opens in theaters. A film shown again is called '재개봉'. In shopping, the sense of opening a package shows up in '개봉 상품' (opened item) and '미개봉' (unopened). For opening a box or letter in speech, '열다' or '뜯다' is more natural.

gh: break a seal, or release a film

t90.ax: That movie will be released next week.

examples.en: This drama is broadcast on terrestrial TV.

examples.ko: 요즘은 공중파보다 유튜브를 더 많이 봐요.
examples.en: These days I watch YouTube more than terrestrial TV.

examples.ko: 공중파 뉴스는 저녁 여덟 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The terrestrial TV news starts at eight in the evening.
I was very nervous appearing on terrestrial TV for the first time.
The terrestrial broadcasters broadcast the World Cup together.

examples.ko: 케이블이 없어도 공중파는 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even without cable, you can watch terrestrial TV.

explain: 안테나로 전파를 받아 보는 지상파 방송을 일상 대화에서 이렇게도 불러요. 케이블 채널, 종합편성채널, 유튜브와 구분할 때 자주 써요. 공식적인 말은 '지상파'예요.

phrases.en: I saw that news on terrestrial broadcast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 케이블이나 인터넷이 아닌 일반 TV 방송을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means regular TV broadcasts, not cable or internet.

phrases.example: 공중파 채널은 안테나로도 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can watch terrestrial channels with an antenna too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채널 하나하나를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to individual channels.

phrases.en: That drama airs on terrestrial TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공중파'와 같은 뜻의 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The formal word with the same meaning as '공중파'.

explain_en: In everyday talk, people also use this word for over-the-air broadcasting. It is often used to separate it from cable channels, general programming channels and YouTube. The formal term is '지상파'.

examples.en: The dancheong of that temple is really colorful.
I took many photos of the dancheong at Gyeongbokgung.

examples.ko: 단청을 새로 해서 건물이 산뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: They repainted the dancheong, so the building looks fresh.

examples.ko: 한국의 전통 건물에는 단청이 칠해져 있어요.
examples.en: Traditional Korean buildings have dancheong painted on them.

examples.ko: 단청 색깔이 바랜 곳은 다시 칠한대요.
examples.en: I hear they will repaint the parts where the dancheong colors have faded.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구에게 단청의 아름다움을 설명해 줬어요.
examples.en: I explained the beauty of dancheong to my foreign friend.

explain: 궁궐이나 절 같은 전통 건물의 처마와 기둥에 그린 색 무늬를 말해요. 여행이나 문화 수업에서 자주 나오고, '단청을 입히다/칠하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 장인들이 절의 기둥에 단청을 칠하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Craftsmen are painting dancheong on the temple pillars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전통 건물에 색 무늬를 그리는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for painting colorful patterns on a traditional building.

phrases.en: The colorful dancheong caught my eye right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단청의 색이 다채롭고 눈에 띌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the colors of dancheong are vivid and eye-catching.

phrases.en: The dancheong of this palace is really beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단청의 색과 무늬가 아름답다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise the beautiful colors and patterns.

explain_en: It refers to the colorful patterns painted on the eaves and pillars of traditional buildings such as palaces and temples. It comes up in travel and culture classes, and you say '단청을 입히다/칠하다'.

examples.en: In art class, we made a mosaic from colored paper.
There is a beautiful mosaic on the cathedral wall.
On the broadcast, they covered the face with pixelation.
I pixelated the license plate in the photo.

examples.ko: 작은 타일을 붙여 모자이크 그림을 완성했어요.
examples.en: We finished a mosaic picture by sticking on small tiles.
There is a mosaic-like pattern on the floor.

explain: 작은 조각을 붙여 만든 그림 말고도, 한국에서는 영상이나 사진의 일부를 네모 모양으로 흐리게 가리는 것도 '모자이크'라고 해요. '모자이크하다', '모자이크 처리하다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: blur out (a part of an image)
phrases.nuance_ko: 영상이나 사진에서 얼굴, 번호 같은 부분을 알아볼 수 없게 가린다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Hiding parts such as faces or numbers in an image so they cannot be recognized.

explain_en: Besides a picture made of small pieces, Koreans also call blurring part of a photo or video into blocks '모자이크'. People say '모자이크하다' or '모자이크 처리하다' for this.

en: to be preserved; to be conserved

examples.ko: 이 건물은 옛 모습 그대로 보존돼요.
examples.en: This building is preserved just as it used to look.
The dinosaur bones were well preserved underground.

examples.ko: 냉동실에 넣으면 음식이 더 오래 보존될 거예요.
examples.en: Food will keep longer if you put it in the freezer.

examples.ko: 잘 보존되는 문화재는 관리하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Well-preserved cultural properties have many people looking after them.

examples.ko: 자연이 보존되고 나서 새들이 다시 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: After nature was preserved, the birds came back.

examples.ko: 사진이 잘 보존돼서 백 년 전 모습을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: The photos are well preserved, so we can see how it looked a hundred years ago.

explain: '보관되다'는 어디에 두었는지가 중요하고, '보존되다'는 원래 상태가 변하지 않았다는 점이 중요해요. 문화재, 자연, 식품, 자료에 많이 써요. 사람이 하면 '보존하다', 그 결과로 남아 있으면 '보존되다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 그림은 오백 년 동안 잘 보존됐어요.
phrases.en: This painting has been well preserved for five hundred years.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘'을 붙이면 상태가 거의 변하지 않았다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: '잘' makes clear that the condition has barely changed.

phrases.example: 그 집은 옛 모습이 보존되지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That house's original look was not preserved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 모습이 남지 않고 달라졌을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used when the original look didn't survive.

phrases.en: The old village remains just as it was.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보존되다'의 쉬운 말로, 변하지 않고 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say something remains unchanged, like '보존되다'.

explain_en: '보관되다' focuses on where something is kept, while '보존되다' focuses on the original condition not changing. It is common with cultural assets, nature, food and records. A person does '보존하다'; the result is '보존되다'.

en: to be restored; to be reconstructed

examples.ko: 불에 탄 옛 성이 다시 복원됐어요.
examples.en: The old castle that burned down was restored.
I'm glad the deleted file was restored safely.

examples.ko: 오래된 그림이 복원되는 과정을 영상으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of how an old painting gets restored.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 내년에 원래 모습으로 복원될 거예요.
examples.en: This building will be restored to its original look next year.

examples.ko: 문화재가 복원되면 많은 사람이 찾아올 것 같아요.
examples.en: Once the cultural property is restored, I think many people will visit.

examples.ko: 복원된 사진 속 할머니는 정말 젊고 예뻤어요.
examples.en: The grandmother in the restored photo was really young and pretty.

explain: 건물, 그림, 문화재, 파일처럼 망가지거나 사라진 것을 원래 모습으로 되돌릴 때 써요. '수리되다'는 고장 난 물건에 쓰고, '복원되다'는 옛 모습을 되찾는 느낌이 강해요. 하는 쪽은 '복원하다'예요.

phrases.en: The old painting was restored to its original look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 모습을 되찾는다는 느낌을 분명하게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear the sense of regaining the former look.
phrases.en_equiv: to be restored to its original form

phrases.en: The restoration of the cultural property is in full swing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문화재나 건물을 되살리는 일을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the work of bringing back a cultural asset or building.

phrases.en: The data hasn't been restored yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 되돌리지 못했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say it has not been brought back yet.

explain_en: Used when something damaged or lost, like a building, painting, cultural property or file, gets back its original form. 수리되다 fits broken things being fixed, while 복원되다 stresses getting the old look back. The active form is 복원하다.

t90.ax: The old castle that burned down was restored.

examples.en: The dove is a symbol of peace.
The Korean flag symbolizes the spirit of our country.
Red is a color that is seen as a symbol of passion.

examples.ko: 이 탑은 우리 도시의 역사로 상징돼서 관광객이 많아요.
examples.en: This tower is seen as a symbol of the city's history, so it has many tourists.
The heart came to be a symbol of love.
Think about what it will be symbolized by.

explain: 'A는 B로 상징된다'처럼 조사 '로'와 같이 써요. 상징하는 대상이 주어이고, 책이나 뉴스, 발표에서 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 'A 하면 B가 떠올라요'처럼 풀어서 많이 해요.

phrases.en: A heart symbolizes love.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상징되다'의 능동형으로, 상징이 되는 대상이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form; the symbol itself is the subject.

phrases.en: This place has symbolic meaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 뜻을 대신 보여 준다는 느낌으로 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to say that something stands for a meaning.

phrases.en: The tiger is a symbol of Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 동사보다 이 명사 표현이 더 쉽고 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, this noun phrase is easier and more natural than the verb.

explain_en: Used in the pattern 'A는 B로 상징된다' with the particle '로'. The thing that stands for something is the subject. It shows up in books, news and presentations; in speech people often say 'A 하면 B가 떠올라요'.

examples.en: That athlete was disqualified for committing a foul.

examples.ko: 출발 신호 전에 뛰면 바로 실격돼요.
examples.en: If you run before the start signal, you're disqualified right away.

examples.ko: 시험 시간에 휴대폰을 쓰면 실격될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you use a phone during the exam, you can be disqualified.
I heard he was disqualified from the contest because of missing documents.

examples.ko: 실격된 팀은 상을 받을 수 없어요.
examples.en: A disqualified team can't receive a prize.
If you break the rules, do you really get disqualified?

explain: 경기, 대회, 시험에서 규칙을 어겨 자격을 잃을 때 써요. 억울하거나 안타까운 느낌을 더할 때는 '실격당하다'라고도 하고, 명사 '실격'과 '실격 처리'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I was disqualified for breaking the rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실격되다'보다 억울하거나 안타까운 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds a sense of unfairness or regret compared to 'silgyeokdoeda'.

phrases.en: If you arrive late, you are treated as disqualified.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙에 따라 공식적으로 실격으로 정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being officially counted as disqualified under the rules.

phrases.en: If you follow the rules, you won't be disqualified.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 괜찮다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say someone is safe.

explain_en: It is used when someone loses eligibility in a game, contest or exam by breaking rules. To add a sense of unfairness or pity you can say '실격당하다', and the noun '실격' and the phrase '실격 처리' are also common.

en: to be derived from; to originate

examples.en: This food originated in China.
Where does the word 'kimchi' come from?

examples.ko: 한국어 단어 중 일부는 영어에서 유래돼요.
examples.en: Some Korean words derive from English.

examples.ko: 이 축제는 옛날 농사 풍습에서 유래된 거예요.
examples.en: This festival comes from an old farming custom.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 어느 나라에서 유래되었는지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you know which country this song originated in?
I was curious how the name came about.

explain: 말, 음식, 풍습이 어디에서 시작되었는지를 말할 때 써요. '~에서 유래되다'로 쓰고, 시작된 곳이나 원인이 앞에 와요. 명사 '유래'는 '이 말의 유래'처럼 시작이나 내력을 가리키고, '어원'은 단어가 어디서 왔는지를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Do you know the origin of this name?
phrases.nuance_ko: '유래되다'의 명사형으로, 어떻게 시작됐는지 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form, used to ask how something started.

phrases.en: This word originates from English.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유래되다'와 뜻이 같고, 주어가 시작을 직접 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 유래되다, with the subject stated directly.

phrases.en: This is a food that originated in Japan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '~에서 시작된'이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, it means 'that began in ~'.

explain_en: Use it for where a word, food or custom started. It goes as ~에서 유래되다, with the starting place or source in front. The noun 유래 means the origin or history, as in '이 말의 유래', while 어원 is specifically a word's etymology.

examples.en: That incident needs to be re-examined.

examples.ko: 이 다큐는 잊힌 독립운동가의 재조명에 큰 역할을 했어요.
examples.en: This documentary played a big role in bringing a forgotten independence activist back into focus.

examples.ko: 옛 가요가 재조명을 받으면서 다시 인기를 얻고 있어요.
examples.en: Old songs are regaining popularity as they get a fresh look.

examples.ko: 역사학계에서는 그 인물의 재조명 작업이 한창이에요.
examples.en: In the history field, work to reassess that figure is in full swing.

examples.ko: 재조명 열풍 덕분에 오래된 책이 다시 팔려요.
examples.en: Thanks to the craze for revisiting the past, old books are selling again.

examples.ko: 재조명의 계기가 된 것은 한 편의 영화였어요.
examples.en: What triggered the renewed attention was a single film.

explain: '재조명을 받다', '재조명이 이루어지다'처럼 과거의 인물, 사건, 작품이 새롭게 다시 평가될 때 써요. 뉴스와 방송에서 자주 나오는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '다시 보다' 정도로 말해요. 동사는 '재조명하다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 화가의 작품이 최근 재조명을 받고 있어요.
phrases.en: This painter's works are receiving renewed attention recently.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 것이 다시 주목받는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something from the past gets attention again.

phrases.en: The incident was reassessed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 살펴보고 평가하는 일이 진행될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a fresh look and evaluation takes place.

phrases.example: 이 영화가 그 시대 재조명의 계기가 됐어요.
phrases.en: This film became an occasion to revisit that era.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 주목받게 된 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the reason something gets renewed attention.

explain_en: It is used when a past person, event or work gets evaluated anew, as in '재조명을 받다' and '재조명이 이루어지다'. It appears often in news and broadcasts, while in daily talk people say something like '다시 보다'. The verb form is '재조명하다'.

examples.ko: 이 놀이는 오래전부터 우리나라에 전래돼 왔어요.
examples.en: This game has been handed down in our country for a long time.
Buddhism was introduced to Korea by way of China.

examples.ko: 전래되는 이야기에는 옛사람들의 지혜가 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: Stories passed down carry the wisdom of people of old.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 마을에 전래되어서 지금도 불려요.
examples.en: This song was handed down in the village, so it is still sung today.

examples.ko: 외국에서 전래된 음식이 이제는 우리 음식처럼 느껴져요.
examples.en: Food introduced from abroad now feels like our own food.

examples.ko: 전래되는 방법대로 장을 담그는 집이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Fewer households make soy sauce the traditional handed-down way.

explain: 전래되다는 오래된 이야기나 풍습이 대대로 내려올 때, 또 다른 나라에서 들어올 때 모두 써요. '전래 동화', '전래 놀이'처럼 앞에 붙는 말이 되는 경우가 많아요. '전해지다'가 더 일상적이고 말하기에도 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: This story has been handed down since long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 일상적인 말로, 말할 때도 자연스럽게 쓰고 '전래되다'보다 부드러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word that sounds natural in speech and softer than 전래되다.

phrases.en: My grandmother told me a traditional folk tale.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전래'가 앞에 붙은 가장 흔한 합성어로, 옛날부터 내려오는 이야기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common compound with 전래, meaning stories passed down from long ago.

phrases.en: We tried traditional games on the holiday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윷놀이, 제기차기처럼 오래전부터 이어진 놀이를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to games passed down for ages, like yut or jegi-chagi.

explain_en: It fits both customs or tales passed down through generations and things that came in from another country. It often appears before nouns, as in 전래 동화 (folk tale) and 전래 놀이 (traditional game). 전해지다 is more everyday and sounds more natural in casual speech.

examples.en: Today's game is broadcast live on TV.
The final was broadcast around the world.
The concert is being broadcast live.
The live screen keeps cutting out.
This event is not broadcast live.
Shall we watch the game together when it's broadcast?

explain: 스포츠나 행사를 현장에서 바로 보여 줄 때 써요. 일상에서는 명사 '중계'나 '생중계'를 더 자주 들어요. 방송하는 쪽은 '중계하다', 방송되는 경기나 행사 쪽은 중계되다예요.

phrases.en: The final is broadcast live on television.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중계되다'에 '바로 그때'라는 뜻이 더해져서, 일어나는 일을 실시간으로 보여 준다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the sense of 'in real time' to 중계되다, meaning shown as it happens.

phrases.en: The event was relayed on air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 수단으로 중계되는지를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the medium through which something is relayed.

phrases.en: The game is being relayed online right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 방송을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a broadcast that is happening now.

explain_en: It is used when a sport or event is shown live from the scene. In daily life you more often hear the nouns '중계' and '생중계'. The broadcasting side uses '중계하다', while the game or event being shown is '중계되다'.
